existingCatalogue.meaning: Each legacy catalogue entry groups1A,1B,2 question-bank IDs as one set. Do not treat ten new timed papers as ten legacy full-set entries, and do not reuse those bank IDs.

A.1.title: Kinematics
A.1.scope: s,v,a; uniform acceleration; projectile components; motion graphs; drag effects qualitatively
boundaries: Quantitative projectile motion excludes fluid resistance and assumes near-surface constantg.
No required trajectory-equation derivation or calculus solution of drag equations.

A.2.title: Forces and momentum
A.2.scope: Newton laws; friction; Hooke; Stokes drag; buoyancy; impulse; momentum; collisions; circular motion
boundaries: SL quantitative collisions/explosions1D; HL may use2D despite shared topic label.
Do not require simultaneous momentum-and-energy collision equations.
Vertical nonuniform circular-force calculations only at top/bottom; no quantitative banked surfaces.

A.3.title: Work, energy and power
A.3.scope: energy conservation; force-displacement area; kinetic/near-surface gravitational/elastic energy; power; efficiency; fuel energy density

A.4.title: Rigid body mechanics
A.4.scope: torque; rotational equilibrium/kinematics; inertia; angular momentum/impulse; rotational energy
boundaries: Supply distribution-specific inertia formulas when needed; point-mass sum is assessable.
No centre-of-mass calculation or formal vector treatment of torque/angular momentum.
Combined translation/rotation restricted to rolling without slipping.

A.5.title: Galilean and special relativity
A.5.scope: inertial frames; Lorentz coordinates/velocity addition; interval; proper time/length; simultaneity; spacetime diagrams; muons
boundaries: No required derivation of transformations/time dilation/length contraction.
Spacetime vertical axisct; straight constant-velocity worldlines; transformed frame scales are not ordinary Euclidean rotations.
Do not import relativistic momentum/dynamical energy as unstated prior knowledge.

B.1.title: Thermal energy transfers
B.1.scope: particle/internal-energy models; heat capacity/latent heat; conduction/convection/radiation; Stefan-Boltzmann; brightness; Wien
boundaries: Use updated negative sign in directional conduction equation; heat-flow magnitude is positive.

B.2.title: Greenhouse effect
B.2.scope: albedo/emissivity; radiation/absorption spectra; planetary energy balance; atmosphere/surface exchange
boundaries: Account for sphere projected area versus emitting area and state atmospheric-layer assumptions.

B.3.title: Gas laws
B.3.scope: ideal/real gases; pV=nRT; kinetic-pressure model; monatomic internal energy; constantp,V,T processes
boundaries: Kinetic pressure depends on mean squared translational speed, not squared mean speed.
MonatomicU=3nRT/2 is shared, but cyclic engine/adiabatic/first-law assessment belongsB.4HL.

B.4.title: Thermodynamics
B.4.scope: Q=deltaU+W; work andPV area; entropy; microstates; first/second laws; monatomic adiabaticpV^(5/3); cycles/Carnot
boundaries: Q positive into system; W positive done by system.
Quantitative systems limited to monatomic ideal gases; distinguish closed from isolated.
Use entropy Q/T only for an appropriate reversible thermal transfer/reservoir model.

B.5.title: Current and circuits
B.5.scope: dc cells; charge flow; pd/emf/internal resistance; resistivity; ohmic/nonohmic devices; series/parallel; power
boundaries: AC circuits not required; no capacitor/RC or inductance/RL knowledge assumed.
Meters ideal unless a constant nonideal resistance is specified.
Variable resistors restricted to thermistors,LDRs,potentiometers.

C.1.title: Simple harmonic motion
C.1.ahl: phase; sinusoidalx/v; speed-displacement; quantitative kinetic/potential/total energy
boundaries: Do not require AHL phase or energy formulas from SL students.

C.2.title: Wave model
C.2.scope: transverse/longitudinal; f,lambda,T,v; mechanical/EM; displacement-time and displacement-position
boundaries: Diagrams must distinguish particle displacement, propagation and phase.

C.3.title: Wave phenomena
C.3.sl: reflection/refraction/transmission; wavefronts/rays; diffraction qualitative; Snell/critical angle; superposition/coherence; double-source/double-slit interference
C.3.ahl: single-slit angular minimum/intensity pattern; envelope on double slit; multiple slits/gratings
boundaries: Interference/diffraction normal incidence only; single slit rectangular, monochromatic; width-intensity effect qualitative.
No assumed thin-film interference, polarization/Malus, Rayleigh resolution or lens-equation techniques.

C.4.title: Standing waves and resonance
C.4.scope: two opposite identical waves; nodes/antinodes; strings/pipes; phase; driven resonance; light/critical/heavy damping
boundaries: Two-wave superposition only; no pipe end corrections.
Carefully distinguish displacement and pressure nodes in air; use stated end conditions.

C.5.title: Doppler effect
C.5.sl: wavefront representation; sound/EM effect; low-speed light fractional shift; spectral motion
boundaries: No problem with both source and observer moving.
For light use stated low-speed approximation; do not assume a relativistic Doppler equation.

D.1.title: Gravitational fields
D.1.ahl: potential/energy; gradient; equipotentials; escape/circular-orbit speeds/energetics; small-drag effect
boundaries: Numerical orbits circular; resultantg calculations on line joining two masses.
Distinguish common Newton/circular-motion derivation from AHL potential and escape-energy formulas.

D.2.title: Electric and magnetic fields
boundaries: Equipotential collections at most4pointcharges; include solid/hollow conducting spheres and plates.
Magnetic field patterns: bar magnet, straight wire, circular coil, air-core solenoid.

D.3.title: Motion in electromagnetic fields
boundaries: Magnetic force changes direction, not kinetic energy; retain charge sign for direction.

D.4.title: Induction
boundaries: Quantitative straight conductors perpendicular toB and rectangularcoils entering/leaving/rotating infields.
Self-induction qualitative only; inductance and RL circuits not required; no transformer/RMS/AC-impedance techniques assumed.

E.1.title: Structure of the atom
boundaries: Supply chemical symbols; SL not expected to calculate Rutherford closest approach.

E.2.title: Quantum physics
boundaries: No required Compton derivation; no Schrodinger, uncertainty-principle, tunnelling or particle-in-box machinery assumed.

E.3.title: Radioactive decay
boundaries: Weak nuclear force not considered; do not assume quark/particle classifications.
AHLdecayconstant is probability perunit-time only as small-lambda*t approximation.

E.5.title: Fusion and stars
boundaries: Use outward thermal OR radiation pressure as appropriate, correctedNovember2024.
Cepheid variables not required; no Hubble/cosmology/distance-ladder machinery assumed.
HRaxesluminosityvertical/temperaturehorizontal; state conventional decreasing-temperature direction.

skills.uncertainty: absolute/fractional/percentage; arithmetic/powers; best-fit versus max/min gradients and intercepts; appropriate precision
skills.graphs: units/scales; errorbars; linearization/logscales; gradient/area; physicalintercepts; comparemodels
skills.investigation: control/calibration; random/systematicerror; precisionvsaccuracy; causalexplanation; relevantimprovements; avoidgeneric'humanerror'
skills.mathematics: algebra/trigonometry/logs/exponentials; ratios/estimation;2Dvectorcomponents; graphicalrates/areas. No calculus, ODEsolving or advancedstatistics should be presumed.
skills.novelContexts: May supply an unfamiliar relationship as part of a data-based question and assess stated skills; label that relationship and supply all needed information.

marking.mcq: one correct A-D option,1mark,no penalty; independent solve and distractor analysis required
marking.written: positive awardable points; full working; equivalent valid methods/wording accepted; explicit linked dependencies and ECF where appropriate
marking.unitsAndPrecision: Carry sensible SI units/signs and appropriate significant figures. Do not create an automatic deduction at every step; any specific unit/precision requirement must be stated.
marking.alternatives: Represent OR methods as alternatives, never add all alternative points to the available total.
marking.internalCodes: M1/A1/R1 may serve portal scoring; they are internal organization, not a claim that official Physics schemes use the AA coding system.
marking.gradeBoundaries: Do not invent official 2026 grade boundaries for original mocks or label uncalibrated difficulty as an empirical grade predictor.

authoringPolicy.sourceGuidance: Specific native page anchors; new wording/data, meaningful changed reasoning and scientifically accurate regenerated figures; no source scan extraction as a student figure
authoringPolicy.data: Synthetic experimental data explicitly presented as model/laboratory data; internally consistent units/uncertainties; no false claim of a named real study
authoringPolicy.verification: Fresh per-part solves, numeric tolerances, dimensions, limiting cases, uniqueness/domain checks, diagram-data matching, distractor uniqueness; separate author and independent review; final PDF/native visual QA
